clue.text: Look for attention in school

indicators.note: in places the word for attention inside the abbreviation for school

parts.note: to have someone's ear is to have their attention

explanation.surface: A pupil is asked to seek out a teacher's attention during lessons.
explanation.definitionFit: To search is to hunt or seek, the same as looking for something.

clue.text: Actions taken by a traveller

parts.note: a suit is a lawsuit, a legal action
a case is also a legal action brought in court

explanation.surface: Things done by someone on a journey.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Actions' gives both pieces: the two words for a legal action, one after the other. The definition is the thing a traveller takes along.
explanation.definitionFit: A travelling bag is what a traveller carries with clothes inside, so it is the item taken on a trip.

clue.text: Keeper to a monarch in his prime

parts.note: R stands for Rex or Regina, a reigning monarch
someone in their prime is fully grown, at full adult strength

explanation.surface: A guardian is assigned to a king at the height of his powers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Keeper' is not a guard: it is the bar of soft iron laid across a magnet's poles, also called by this name.
explanation.definitionFit: In magnetism a keeper is the iron piece across a magnet's poles, which is another name for this component.

clue.text: Tightening one's belt? An easy task in Gateshead

parts.note: a cinch is something very easy to do
read as 'Gate's head', the first letter of gate

explanation.surface: Economising is said to be no trouble for people living in Gateshead, a town in north-east England.
explanation.walkthrough: Gateshead is a town in north-east England, but split as 'Gate's head' it gives just G.
explanation.definitionFit: A cinch is a saddle girth, and pulling a belt tight is drawing it in, as a girth is drawn in.

clue.text: Small child at first rebuked and rejected

parts.note: S is the usual abbreviation for small, as on clothing labels

indicators.note: at first signals only the opening letter of the word child

parts.note: to rap someone is to rebuke them sharply

explanation.surface: A little one was told off and then pushed away.
explanation.definitionFit: Something scrapped has been thrown out or discarded as unwanted.

clue.text: Scrooges favourite fish?

parts.note: a miser like Scrooge would favour a flatfish that costs little, an inexpensive ray

explanation.surface: Which seafood would a notorious miser enjoy most?
explanation.walkthrough: Scrooge is Dickens's miser; a skate is a flatfish, and one that is cheap suits him, while the two words together name a stingy person.
explanation.definitionFit: A stingy person who hates spending money, like Scrooge, is called by this word.

clue.text: Houses Jack plus poems

parts.note: a jack is a sailor, and AB (able seaman) is the usual crossword sailor
odes are lyric poems

explanation.surface: Someone named Jack produces dwellings and verses.
explanation.definitionFit: Abodes are dwellings or homes, the places where people live.

clue.text: Let my hair have waves!

parts.note: a perm puts lasting waves or curls into hair
the hair is referred to as it, as in 'curl it'

explanation.surface: A customer at the hairdresser demands curls.
explanation.walkthrough: Read the whole exclamation as an order to the stylist about the hair: curl it with a perm. Then the opening word alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To let something happen is to allow or authorise it.

clue.text: Said French female appears to vacillate

parts.note: dit is French for said
her is a female pronoun

explanation.surface: A Frenchwoman who spoke seems undecided.
explanation.definitionFit: To dither is to waver indecisively, hovering between choices.

clue.text: I am awfully mean and brutish

parts.note: I am contracts to I'm

indicators.note: awfully suggests the letters are badly arranged and must be put in a new order

explanation.surface: Someone confesses to being dreadfully nasty and savage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'awfully' rearranges IM (I'm, the short form of 'I am') with MEAN. The answer is an archaic word for monstrously cruel.
explanation.definitionFit: An archaic adjective for monstrously cruel or savage, close to brutal.

clue.text: Tom cared about being an opponent of tyranny

indicators.note: about here means moved around, so the letters of the two words are shuffled

explanation.surface: A man called Tom worried about becoming a foe of despots.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' rearranges the letters of TOM and CARED together.
explanation.definitionFit: A believer in rule by the people stands against despotic rule.

clue.text: Musical round youngsters initially find captivating

parts.note: a catch is a round, a song sung in canon

indicators.note: initially signals the first letter of the word youngsters

explanation.surface: A tune sung in rounds that children enjoy at once.
explanation.definitionFit: A tune that is easy to remember and appealing is described by this adjective.

clue.text: Withdrawn secretary with little enthusiasm

indicators.note: withdrawn means drawn back, so the letters for secretary are read backwards

parts.note: a PA is a personal assistant, a secretary
petite means small or dainty

explanation.surface: A shy office assistant shows little keenness for the job.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Withdrawn' looks like a description of a shy secretary, but it is the reversal signal; 'little' is the adjective meaning small and dainty.
explanation.definitionFit: A hunger or keen desire for something is a kind of eagerness or relish.

clue.text: A second-rate answer requires indulgence

parts.note: B is second class, second-rate after A
a solution is an answer to a problem

explanation.surface: A mediocre reply calls for some leniency from the examiner.
explanation.definitionFit: In the church an indulgence is a remission of punishment for sins, like a pardon forgiving them.

clue.text: Seasonal hamper expressly for rugby team

indicators.note: expressly read as expressed in speech, so the words are said out loud

parts.note: a hamper for the season after winter: spring box

explanation.surface: A festive food basket prepared specially for a rugby side.
explanation.walkthrough: 'expressly' is read as 'in speech': a spring box spoken out loud sounds like the name of South Africa's national rugby union team.
explanation.definitionFit: South Africa's national rugby union side is known by this name, after the antelope.

clue.text: Succeeded in getting damage repaired

definitions.meaning: to make good is to prosper or do well in life
to make good damage is to put right or repair it

explanation.surface: Someone did well by having harm fixed.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means both prospered in life and put right or compensated for harm done.

clue.text: Navigational bar in Italian navigator's time

parts.note: John Cabot (Giovanni Caboto) was the Italian navigator who reached North America in 1497
an age is a period of time

explanation.surface: A Renaissance explorer's era saw barriers to sailing.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is coastal shipping and the restriction of it to a country's own vessels, the 'bar' on foreign carriers.
explanation.definitionFit: The term covers coastal trade and the rule barring foreign ships or aircraft from domestic routes.

clue.text: Visionary offers detailed suggestions

parts.note: an idea is a suggestion
to list things is to detail them one by one

explanation.surface: A forward-thinker puts forward full proposals.
explanation.walkthrough: 'detailed suggestions' reads as ideas set out in a list.
explanation.definitionFit: A visionary pursues high ideals and imagines things better than they are.

clue.text: Opposed to pop group taking drugs, maybe

parts.note: contra is Latin for against
a band is a group of musicians

explanation.surface: Being against a pop group for using narcotics.
explanation.definitionFit: Smuggled or illegal goods, of which illicit narcotics are an example.

clue.text: When enraptured, win approval

parts.note: as can mean when, as in 'as he left'
sent is slang for thrilled or carried away

explanation.surface: Someone thrilled by the moment earns agreement.
explanation.definitionFit: Assent is agreement or consent given to a proposal.

clue.text: A wise man orders spring water in saloon

indicators.note: in shows the word for spring water going inside the word for saloon

parts.note: a saloon is the British name for a sedan car
a spa is a mineral spring

explanation.surface: One of the Magi orders mineral water in a bar.
explanation.walkthrough: Saloon is not a bar but a car (British for a sedan). Tradition names three Magi; this is one of them.
explanation.definitionFit: Tradition names him as one of the three Magi who brought gifts to the infant Jesus.

clue.text: It's left for a member initially articulate, clever and young

parts.note: a leg is a limb, a member of the body

indicators.note: initially takes the first letter of each of the three adjectives

explanation.surface: A bequest goes to a young, bright and well-spoken relative.
explanation.walkthrough: 'It's left' means something left in a will, not the opposite of right.
explanation.definitionFit: A bequest is something left to heirs in a will.

clue.text: Assumed a form had got on well

definitions.meaning: taken on a definite shape or developed
made good progress or performed satisfactorily

explanation.surface: Something took shape and made good progress.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrasal verb means both took on a shape and progressed or improved satisfactorily.

clue.text: Ideal hat for the iron lady

parts.note: Fe is the chemical symbol for iron
Dora is a woman's name

explanation.surface: The best headgear for Margaret Thatcher, nicknamed the Iron Lady.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the iron lady' recalls Margaret Thatcher, the British prime minister, but splits into iron (FE) and a lady's name.
explanation.definitionFit: A soft felt hat with a creased crown and brim is a kind of headwear.

clue.text: Quite positive it's time chap reformed

indicators.note: reformed means formed again, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone is sure that a fellow has changed his ways.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reformed' rearranges the letters of TIME and CHAP.
explanation.definitionFit: Being forcefully certain, stressing a point strongly.

clue.text: African therefore goes to another African country

parts.note: so means therefore
Mali is a country in West Africa

explanation.surface: Someone from Africa thus travels to a different nation there.
explanation.definitionFit: A person from Somalia in the Horn of Africa is an African.

clue.text: Loitering whilst attempting to ensnare a redhead

indicators.note: to ensnare means to trap inside, so the word for attempting surrounds the letters

parts.note: trying means attempting
read as the head of red, its first letter

explanation.surface: Someone hangs about hoping to trap a ginger-haired person.
explanation.walkthrough: 'redhead' is not a person but the first letter of red.
explanation.definitionFit: Tarrying is lingering or delaying, staying somewhere longer than needed.

clue.text: Bill takes a breather on arrival

parts.note: an ad is an advertisement, a bill or poster
a vent is an opening for breathing or air

explanation.surface: A man named Bill pauses for rest when he gets there.
explanation.definitionFit: An advent is a coming or arrival, especially of something important.
